away.name: Dylan Garand
away.news: Since Jonas Korpisalo made his season debut earlier this month after returning from a lower-body injury, the Rangers have alternated goalies and will continue that trend on Friday, with Garand tending the twine. The 24-year-old Garand was serviceable in his most recent outing, saving 17 of 19 shots (.895 SV%), but fell 3-1 to the Edmonton Oilers. He has allowed three or fewer goals in five straight games (2-3-0), posting a .915 SV%. The Rangers enter Friday's game as sizeable -213 road favourites against a Vancouver Canucks team that has scored two or fewer goals in five of their last six games (0-6-0).

away.name: Juuse Saros
away.news: Saros has had consecutive disappointing seasons, finishing with a sub-.900 SV% the first two times in his career. That said, he is impressing early in the 2026-27 season, and he is coming off his first shutout, saving 30 shots in a 3-0 win over the Los Angeles Kings. The 31-year-old Finnish goalie has won three straight games, saving 84 of 86 shots (.977 SV%). The Predators enter Friday's game as +136 road underdogs against a Vegas Golden Knights team with points in five straight games (4-0-1).

home.name: Adin Hill
home.news: The Golden Knights have had a liberal goalie rotation in recent weeks and will continue that trend on Friday, turning to Adin Hill. The 30-year-old Hill was excellent in his most recent outing, saving 28 of 29 shots (.966 SV%) in a 4-1 win over the Buffalo Sabres. He has allowed two or fewer goals in three of his past four games (3-1-0). The Golden Knights enter Friday's game as -151 home favourites against a surging Nashville Predators team that has outscored opponents 22-11 during a six-game winning streak.
